reference.title: Cable One Arm Biceps Curl (version 2)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read; the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you curl the handle up, breathe in as you lower it.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, short squeeze, 2-3 s down

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.rest: 60-90 s (or work the other arm in between)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can curl with the elbow still at your side for every rep.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack; slower lowering

cues.text: Face the low pulley, feet hip width, knees soft; hold the D-handle in the right hand, palm forward, arm straight and the elbow at your side. Left hand on the hip.
Breathe out and curl the handle toward the shoulder, moving only at the elbow.
Squeeze the biceps with the palm facing up and back; the elbow stays by your ribs.
Breathe in and lower slowly until the arm is straight again, keeping tension on the cable.
Brief pause with the arm straight, trunk still, then repeat. Switch arms after the set.

mistakes.mistake: Elbow drifting forward as the hand rises
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow pinned to your side; stop the curl when the forearm can go no higher without the elbow moving.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back or twisting to swing the handle up
mistakes.fix: Stand tall with the hips square to the pulley; lighten the stack.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the handle snap back down
mistakes.fix: Lower over 2-3 s to a straight arm, keeping the cable taut.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the wrist to finish the curl
mistakes.fix: Keep the wrist straight in line with the forearm.

kinematics.norm: Full range: mean elbow range was about 117-123 degrees across barbell, EZ-bar and alternating dumbbell curls (Marcolin 2018)
Elbow stays near the side; a big forward swing shifts work to the front deltoid (clinical opinion)
The supinated grip gave the highest biceps activity in the lifting phase (Coratella 2023)
Low pulley in front of the athlete, cable in line with the working hand (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2-3 s down (clinical opinion); biceps activity was lower while lowering than lifting at the same load (Oliveira 2009)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain in the elbow or shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with the elbow still.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Elbow pain at the bottom: stop a little short of a fully straight arm (clinical opinion).
Wrist discomfort: use a neutral (hammer) grip on a rope end instead of the D-handle.
regressions: Two-arm cable curl with a straight bar.
progressions: Bayesian cable curl (facing away from the pulley, arm behind the body; compared with dumbbell curls by Parpa 2025).

muscleNotes.biceps_r: Prime mover: bends the elbow and turns the palm up against the cable. The cable keeps some tension at the bottom, where a dumbbell's load is small.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the handle and help bend the elbow (brachioradialis share rises with a neutral grip, Coratella 2023).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the upper arm still so the elbow does not swing forward.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk upright against the one-sided pull.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the cable's pull rotating and bending the trunk toward the working side.

guides.label: Elbow fully bent at the top
